questions.prompt: Test whether \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\) are linearly independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
From \(a(1,0)+b(0,1)=(0,0)\), component equations give \(a=0,b=0\).
Final answer: The vectors are linearly independent.

questions.prompt: Test whether \((1,2)\) and \((2,4)\) are linearly independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Since \((2,4)=2(1,2)\), the nontrivial relation \(2(1,2)-(2,4)=0\) exists.
Final answer: The vectors are linearly dependent.

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(1,x,x^2\) are linearly independent in \(P_2\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(a+bx+cx^2=0\) for all \(x\), equality of coefficients gives \(a=b=c=0\).
Final answer: \(1,x,x^2\) are linearly independent.

Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The third vector is the sum of the first two, so
\[(1,1,0)+(0,1,1)-(1,2,1)=0.\]

questions.prompt: Determine all \(k\) for which \((1,k)\) and \((2,3)\) are dependent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The column determinant is
\[\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\k&3\end{vmatrix}=3-2k.\]
Dependence requires \(3-2k=0\).
Final answer: \(k=3/2\).

questions.prompt: Test independence of \(1+x\), \(x+x^2\), and \(1-x^2\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For \(a(1+x)+b(x+x^2)+c(1-x^2)=0\), coefficients give \(a+c=0\), \(a+b=0\), \(b-c=0\). These allow \((a,b,c)=(1,-1,-1)\ne0\).
Final answer: The polynomials are linearly dependent.

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) are linearly independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(a\sin x+b\cos x=0\) for all \(x\), set \(x=0\) to get \(b=0\), then \(x=\pi/2\) to get \(a=0\).
Final answer: \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) are linearly independent.

questions.prompt: Find all \(k\) for which \((1,1,0),(0,1,1),(1,k,1)\) are dependent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The determinant of the column matrix is
\[\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&k\\0&1&1\end{vmatrix}=2-k.\]
Set it to zero.
Final answer: \(k=2\).

questions.prompt: Test independence of the matrices \(E_{11},E_{12},E_{21},E_{22}\) in \(M_2(\mathbb R)\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(aE_{11}+bE_{12}+cE_{21}+dE_{22}=0\), the four matrix entries give \(a=b=c=d=0\).
Final answer: The four matrices are linearly independent.

questions.prompt: Determine the dependence relation among four vectors in \(\mathbb R^3\): \(\mathbf e_1,\mathbf e_2,\mathbf e_3,(1,1,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The fourth vector equals the sum of the first three:
\[\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3-(1,1,1)=0.\]
Final answer: The set is dependent with coefficients \((1,1,1,-1)\).

questions.prompt: Determine the rank of the set \((1,2,1),(2,4,2),(0,1,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The second vector is twice the first. The first and third are not scalar multiples, so they are independent.
Final answer: The rank is \(2\).

questions.prompt: Determine all \(k\) for which \(1+x\), \(x+kx^2\), and \(1+x^2\) are independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Their coefficient-column determinant is
\[\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&0\\0&k&1\end{vmatrix}=1+k.\]
Independence requires \(1+k\ne0\).
Final answer: The polynomials are independent for \(k\ne-1\).

questions.prompt: Construct a maximal independent subset of \(\{(1,0,1),(0,1,1),(1,1,2),(1,-1,0)\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The third vector is the sum of the first two, and the fourth is their difference. The first two are independent.
Final answer: One maximal independent subset is \(\{(1,0,1),(0,1,1)\}\).

questions.prompt: Determine all \(k\) for which the columns of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\1&0&k\end{pmatrix}\) are independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
\[\det A=1(1\cdot k-0)-1(0\cdot k-1)=k+1.\]
The columns are independent exactly when the determinant is nonzero.
Final answer: \(k\ne-1\).

questions.prompt: Verify independence of \(e^x,e^{-x}\) using values and derivatives at \(x=0\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(ae^x+be^{-x}=0\), then at zero \(a+b=0\). Differentiating gives \(ae^x-be^{-x}=0\), so at zero \(a-b=0\). Hence \(a=b=0\).
Final answer: \(e^x,e^{-x}\) are linearly independent.

questions.prompt: Prove that a set containing the zero vector is linearly dependent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(\mathbf0\) is the \(j\)-th vector, choose coefficient \(c_j=1\) and every other coefficient zero. Then
\[\sum_i c_i\mathbf v_i=1\mathbf0=\mathbf0\]
is a nontrivial relation.
Final answer: Every set containing \(\mathbf0\) is linearly dependent.

questions.prompt: Prove that eigenvectors belonging to distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Suppose \(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i\mathbf v_i=0\) is a shortest nontrivial relation and \(T\mathbf v_i=\lambda_i\mathbf v_i\). Apply \(T-\lambda_n I\):
\[\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}c_i(\lambda_i-\lambda_n)\mathbf v_i=0.\]
Distinct eigenvalues make every factor nonzero, contradicting minimality unless all \(c_i=0\).
Final answer: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

questions.prompt: Prove that any set of more than \(n\) vectors in \(\mathbb R^n\) is linearly dependent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Place the vectors as columns of an \(n\times m\) matrix with \(m>n\). Its rank is at most \(n<m\), so the homogeneous system \(A\mathbf c=0\) has at least one free variable and a nonzero solution.
Final answer: Every set of more than \(n\) vectors in \(\mathbb R^n\) is dependent.

questions.prompt:
Prove that if \(S\) is independent and \(\mathbf v
otin\operatorname{span}S\), then \(S\cup\{\mathbf v\}\) is independent.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Suppose \(a\mathbf v+\sum_i c_i\mathbf s_i=0\). If \(a\ne0\), then \(\mathbf v=-a^{-1}\sum_i c_i\mathbf s_i\in\operatorname{span}S\), a contradiction. Thus \(a=0\), and independence of \(S\) gives every \(c_i=0\).
Final answer: \(S\cup\{\mathbf v\}\) is linearly independent.
